question.:question/problem: Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}-6\left(\frac{x}{4y+1}\right)\text{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j\,$ for $\frac{8}{3}\le t\le \frac{11}{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $r(t)=t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j,$ then along the curve we have $x=t$ and $y={t}^{2}.$ 

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =i+2tj \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, if  $f(x,y)=-6\left(\frac{x}{4y+1}\right)$, then we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =-6\left(\frac{t}{4{t}^{2}+1}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}-6\left(\frac{x}{4y+1}\right)\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{11}{2}}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t  \\    & =-6\left({\int }_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{11}{2}}(\frac{t}{4{t}^{2}+1})\cdot \sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \text{d}t\right) \\    & =-6\left({\int }_{\frac{8}{3}}^{\frac{11}{2}}\frac{t}{\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+1}}\text{d}t\right).\end{aligned}
$$
